_meta.indication: Treatment of seizures associated with Dravet syndrome (DS) in patients 2 years of age and older taking clobazam. There are no clinical data to support use as monotherapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter (14 centers in France), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of stiripentol vs placebo, add-on to optimized valproate and clobazam; 4-week baseline followed by 8-week double-blind treatment.
pivotal_trials.population: Refractory Dravet syndrome patients ages 3 to 18 years taking both clobazam and valproate, with at least 4 generalized clonic or tonic-clonic seizures per month despite optimized therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of patients who had at least a 50% reduction in monthly seizure frequency from baseline (responder rate; treatment success/failure by Week 12).
pivotal_trials.result: Responder rate 71% on stiripentol vs 5% on placebo (p = 0.0003).

pivotal_trials.phase: Supportive pivotal (category 1) trial; not considered a stand-alone pivotal trial
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter (6 centers in Italy), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of stiripentol vs placebo, add-on to optimized valproate and clobazam; 4-week baseline followed by 8-week double-blind treatment.
pivotal_trials.population: Refractory Dravet syndrome patients ages 3 to 18 years taking both clobazam and valproate, with at least 4 generalized clonic or tonic-clonic seizures per month despite optimized therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of patients who had at least a 50% reduction in monthly seizure frequency from baseline (responder rate).
pivotal_trials.result: Responder rate 67% on stiripentol vs 9% on placebo (nominal p value = 0.0006).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and more frequent than placebo): somnolence (67% vs 23%), decreased appetite (46% vs 10%), decreased weight (27% vs 6%), agitation, ataxia, hypotonia, nausea (15% vs 3%), tremor, dysarthria, and insomnia. Hematologic: neutropenia (13% vs 0%) and thrombocytopenia (12% vs 3%).
target_moa: The mechanism by which stiripentol exerts its anticonvulsant effect in humans is unknown; possible mechanisms include direct effects mediated through the GABA-A receptor and indirect effects involving inhibition of cytochrome P450 (increasing clobazam/norclobazam levels).
modality: Small molecule (aromatic allylic alcohol; new molecular entity)

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented at an Advisory Committee Meeting.

description.text: Expanded to include pediatric patients 6 months to less than 2 years of age weighing 7 kg or more with Dravet syndrome taking clobazam

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for the expansion of the use of Diacomit for the treatment of seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients taking clobazam to include pediatric patients who are 6 months to less than 2 years of age and weighing 7 kg or more.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation for the treatment of Dravet syndrome (FDA orphan designation number 08-2661, granted October 30, 2008).

summary.text: Diacomit (stiripentol), a new molecular entity, was granted FDA orphan designation for Dravet syndrome and received Priority review; it was approved first-cycle (submitted 12/20/17, approved 8/20/18) based on two adequate and well-controlled trials without accelerated approval, breakthrough, or fast track designations.

citations.quote: Stiripentol (STP) is a new molecular entity, and is structurally unrelated to other drugs approved for the treatment of seizures.
STP was granted orphan designation for the treatment of Dravet syndrome by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) (orphan designation number 08-2661) on October 30, 2008
Priority or Standard	Priority
The applicant conducted two adequate and well-controlled trials in DS patients (STICLO France study and STICLO Italy study).
